title: Kūmara and Bacon Hash
description: Orange kūmara parboiled, then crisped in bacon fat and left alone long enough to build a crust. Eggs cooked in wells in the pan so it all comes to the table in one dish.
notes: Kūmara has more sugar in it than a potato, so it colours faster and burns sooner. Keep the pan a shade below where you would run a potato hash and give it the time back instead.

ingredients.name: kūmara
ingredients.note: orange-fleshed sweet potato, peeled and cut into 2 cm dice

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: for a squeeze at the end

steps.text: Parboil the kūmara in salted water for a few minutes until the edges are just yielding, then drain it and leave it to steam dry in the colander.
steps.tip: Steam-dried edges are what crisp later. Damp dice stew in the pan and never colour.

steps.text: Fry the streaky bacon in a heavy pan until the fat has rendered out and the lardons are browning, then add the butter and the onion.
Tip in the kūmara and the smoked paprika, season with flaky salt and black pepper, and press the lot into a single layer.
Leave the hash completely alone until a crust forms underneath, then turn it over in sections rather than stirring it.
steps.tip: Every stir resets the crust. Turn it three times in ten minutes and no more than that.

steps.text: Make four wells in the hash, crack the eggs into them, cover the pan and cook until the whites have just set.
Scatter over the parsley and finish with a squeeze of lemon.
